**Step 1. $T$ bounded below $\Longrightarrow$ $T^*$ is surjective.**

Let $x^* \in X^*$. Define a functional $\phi$ on $T(X) \subseteq Y$ by
$$\phi(Tx) = x^*(x).$$
This is well-defined since $T$ is injective, and it is bounded on $T(X)$ since
$$|\phi(Tx)| = |x^*(x)| \le \|x^*\|\,\|x\| \le \frac{\|x^*\|}{m}\,\|Tx\|.$$
By the Hahn–Banach theorem, $\phi$ extends to some $y^* \in Y^*$ with $\|y^*\| \le \|x^*\|/m$. For this $y^*$,
$$(T^* y^*)(x) = y^*(Tx) = \phi(Tx) = x^*(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in X,$$
so $T^* y^* = x^*$. Since $x^* \in X^*$ was arbitrary, $T^* : Y^* \to X^*$ is surjective.

---

**Step 2. $T^*$ surjective $\Longrightarrow$ $T^{**}$ bounded below.**

Since $T^* : Y^* \to X^*$ is a surjective bounded linear operator between Banach spaces, the Open Mapping Theorem gives a constant $c > 0$ such that for every $x^* \in X^*$ there exists $y^* \in Y^*$ with
$$T^* y^* = x^* \quad \text{and} \quad \|y^*\| \le \frac{1}{c}\|x^*\|.$$

Now let $x^{**} \in X^{**}$. We estimate:
$$\|x^{**}\| = \sup_{\|x^*\| \le 1} |x^{**}(x^*)|.$$
For each $x^* \in X^*$ with $\|x^*\| \le 1$, choose $y^* \in Y^*$ with $T^* y^* = x^*$ and $\|y^*\| \le 1/c$. Then

Taking the supremum over $\|x^*\| \le 1$:
$$\|x^{**}\| \le \frac{1}{c}\,\|T^{**} x^{**}\|,$$
that is,
$$\|T^{**} x^{**}\| \ge c\,\|x^{**}\| \quad \text{for all } x^{**} \in X^{**}.$$

$T^{**}$ is bounded below, hence injective, and the inverse $(T^{**})^{-1} : T^{**}(X^{**}) \to X^{**}$ is bounded (with norm $\le 1/c$). Therefore $T^{**} : X^{**} \to Y^{**}$ is an isomorphism onto its range. $\blacksquare$
